turns.response_html:
That is a standard mechanical outdoor timer, likely being used to automate lighting or a similar hardware project. Setting these up is straightforward once the logic of the pins is clear.

Based on the interface shown in the image, here is how to configure it:

1. Set the Current Time

Rotate the entire dial clockwise until the "TIME NOW" arrow points to the current time of day.

  • Note the AM/PM sectors: The white half of the dial represents daytime hours, while the black half represents nighttime hours.

2. Configure the "On" Cycle

The pins around the edge of the dial control the internal switch.

  • ON (Pins Down): Push the pins down for the duration of time the device should be powered. Each pin usually represents a 30-minute increment.
  • OFF (Pins Up): Pull the pins up for the times the device should remain off.

3. Check the Mode Switch

On the side or bottom (often near where the dial is located), there is usually a manual override switch:

  • Clock Icon / Timer: This enables the programmed schedule.
  • ON: This bypasses the timer and provides constant power to the circuit.

Quick Troubleshooting

  • Obstructions: Ensure the clear plastic cover is snapped shut to prevent debris from jamming the mechanical rotation of the dial.
  • Power Loss: Since this is a mechanical clock, if the main power goes out, the "Time Now" will become inaccurate and will need to be recalibrated manually once power returns.
